summary: Weak keyword co-occurrence match in utility module; no traced exfiltration evidence
details: A keyword co-occurrence pattern matched in lib/Utils/generics.js citing the tokens 'ping', 'GET', and 'id' across separate lines. These tokens individually are common in HTTP utility code (ping/keepalive helpers, GET method strings, message-id fields) and do not by themselves demonstrate exfiltration of installer-side data. No specific installer secret read, no hardcoded attacker destination, and no install-time or import-time auto-execute path is identified from the available evidence. The package name 'sixbails' is consistent with a fork/derivative of the Baileys WhatsApp library family, where such utility modules legitimately appear. Without concrete evidence of installer-targeted data flow to an attacker-controlled endpoint, this is below the block threshold and warrants human review to confirm intent.
